courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Review of Basic Algebra
courses.description: Correctional Education Course. This course covers basic algebra topics and prepares students for an introductory college-level algebra course, such as MATH 110 .

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: First-Year Seminar: 'Fish Gotta Swim, Birds Gotta Fly': The Mathematics and the Mechanics of Moving
courses.description: This seminar allows students to have hands-on exposure to a class of physical and computer experiments designed to challenge intuition on how motion is achieved in nature. Honors version available.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Combinatorics
courses.description: Students will discuss combinatorics' deep roots in history, its connections with the theory of numbers, and its fundamental role for natural science, as well as various applications, including cryptography and the stock market. Honors version available.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Colliding Balls and Springs: The Microstructure of How Materials Behave
courses.description: Students will follow the intellectual journey of the atomic hypothesis from Leucippus and Democritus to the modern era, combining the history, the applications to science, and the mathematics developed to study particles and their interactions.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: First-Year Seminar: The Mathematics of Voting
courses.description: What properties should a fair election have and are these properties achievable in theory and in practice? How can mathematics and statistics be used to expose election fraud and gerrymandering? Students will address these questions as they compare different election systems, evaluate their strengths, weaknesses, and abuses, and design improvements to current structures. Topics will include gerrymandering, ranked voting, approval voting, and Arrow's Impossibility Theorem.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Unfolding Infinity: Mathematical Origami and Fractal Symmetry
courses.description: This seminar engages students in an exploration of the interplay between mathematics, origami, and fractal symmetry. Learning objectives will include mastering basic origami folding techniques, identifying and applying fundamental symmetry operations, recognizing and analyzing fractal symmetry, and creating geometric tessellations. Students will use image editing software (Illustrator and Photoshop), mathematical imaging software (Ultra Fractal), and the laser cutter in UNC's BeAM space, to design and create modular origami and fractal tessellation artwork.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Topology and Symmetry
courses.description: In this seminar, students will explore ideas from topology and geometry and their application to symmetry patterns. Students will learn to identify and classify two-dimensional symmetry patterns and create their own designs. Students will relate symmetry patterns to their folded-up counterparts, called orbifolds, and use tools from topology and geometry to determine which patterns are possible and which patterns can never be achieved.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Special Topics
courses.description: Special topics course. Content will vary each semester. Honors version available.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Algebra
courses.description: Provides a one-semester review of the basics of algebra. Basic algebraic expressions, functions, exponents, and logarithms are included, with an emphasis on problem solving. This course does not satisfy any general education requirements. It is intended for students who need it as a prerequisite for other classes. A student cannot receive credit for this course after receiving credit for MATH 231 or higher.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Algebra Corequisite
courses.description: This course provides just-in-time instruction and practice on basic algebra to support students in Algebra. It also provides additional practice on some of the more difficult topics from MATH 110 . This course is intended for students currently enrolled in MATH 110 who need additional review of algebra.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Reasoning with Data: Navigating a Quantitative World
courses.description: Students will use mathematical and statistical methods to address societal problems, make personal decisions, and reason critically about the world. Authentic contexts may include voting, health and risk, digital humanities, finance, and human behavior. This course does not count as credit towards the psychology or neuroscience majors.

source.text: MATH 115. | 3 Credits. | FC-QUANT. | BIOL 115 , PSYC 115 , STOR 115 .

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Intuitive Calculus
courses.description: Provides an introduction in as nontechnical a setting as possible to the basic concepts of calculus. The course is intended for the nonscience major. A student may not receive credit for this course after receiving credit for MATH 152 or 231 .

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Aspects of Finite Mathematics
courses.description: Introduction to basic concepts of finite mathematics, including topics such as counting methods, finite probability problems, and networks. The course is intended for the nonscience major. A student cannot receive credit for this course after receiving credit for MATH 231 or higher.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Aspects of Modern Mathematics
courses.description: Introduction to mathematical topics of current interest in society and science, such as the mathematics of choice, growth, finance, and shape. The course is intended for the non-science major. A student cannot receive credit for this course after receiving credit for MATH 231 or higher.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Introduction to Mathematical Modeling
courses.description: Provides an introduction to the use of mathematics for modeling real-world phenomena in a nontechnical setting. Models use algebraic, graphical, and numerical properties of elementary functions to interpret data. This course is intended for the nonscience major.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Precalculus Mathematics
courses.description: Awarded as placement credit based on test scores. Does not fulfill a graduation requirement.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Precalculus Mathematics
courses.description: Covers the basic mathematical skills needed for learning calculus. Topics are calculating and working with functions and data, introduction to trigonometry, parametric equations, and the conic sections. A student may not receive credit for this course after receiving credit for MATH 231 .
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisite, MATH 110; a grade of C- or better is required.

source.text: MATH 130. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisite, MATH 110 ; a grade of C- or better is required. | FY-LAUNCH (only designated sections), FC-QUANT.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Calculus for Business and Social Sciences
courses.description: An introductory survey of differential and integral calculus with emphasis on techniques and applications of interest for business and the social sciences. This is a terminal course and not adequate preparation for MATH 232 . A student cannot receive credit for this course after receiving credit for MATH 231 .

source.text: MATH 152. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisite, MATH 110 . | FY-LAUNCH (only designated sections), FC-QUANT.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Special Topics in Mathematics
courses.description: An undergraduate seminar course that is designed to be a participatory intellectual adventure on an advanced, emergent, and stimulating topic within a selected discipline in mathematics. This course does not count as credit towards the mathematics major.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Mathematical Tools for Data Science
courses.description: This course introduces students to the tools of linear algebra and optimization, including solving linear systems, matrices as linear transformations, eigenvalues and eigenvectors, singular value decomposition, derivatives, and the method of gradient descent. Includes applications to data science such as image compression, principal component analysis, and neural networks. Computational tools (e.g. Python) will be used to implement algorithms. No programming experience needed. A student cannot receive credit after receiving credit for MATH 347 or 577 .

source.text: MATH 210. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisite, MATH 110 or 110P. | FC-QUANT.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Calculus of Functions of One Variable I
courses.description: Limits, derivatives, and integrals of functions of one variable. A student cannot receive credit for this course after receiving credit for MATH 152 . Honors version available.

courses.title: Calculus I Corequisite
courses.description: This course provides just-in-time instruction and review on algebra and trigonometry to support students in MATH 231 . It also provides additional practice on some of the more difficult topics from Calculus 1. This course is intended to be taken by students currently enrolled in MATH 231 who need review of algebra and trigonometry.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Calculus of Functions of One Variable II
courses.description: Techniques of integration, numerical integration, applications of integration, improper integrals, sequences, series, power series, Taylor's formula, elementary differential equations. Honors version available. Honors version available.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Calculus of Functions of Several Variables
courses.description: Vector algebra, solid analytic geometry, partial derivatives, multiple integrals. Honors version available.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Mathematics for Data Science
courses.description: This course introduces students to some of the key mathematical tools underlying algorithmic data science. The primary focus of the course is matrix algebra and multivariable calculus. The mathematical topics covered in the course will be motivated and connected by concrete applications in data science, with an emphasis on machine learning and optimization.

source.text: MATH 235. | 4 Credits. | Prerequisites, MATH 231 and MATH 232 . | FC-QUANT. | STOR 235 .

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Special Topics in Mathematics
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. Elective topics in mathematics. This course has variable content and may be taken multiple times for credit.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 6 total credits. 6 total completions.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Undergraduate Learning Assistantships
courses.description: Permission required. Experience includes preparations, demonstrations, assistance, and attendance at weekly meetings, weekly office hours, and class sections. Assistants will not be involved in any aspects of grading. May be repeated for credit.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisite, MATH 231 with a grade of A- or higher; Pre- or corequisite, Permission of Instructor.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Undergraduate Seminar in Mathematics
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. A seminar on a chosen topic in mathematics in which the students participate more actively than in usual courses.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 6 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Directed Exploration in Mathematics
courses.description: By permission of the director of undergraduate studies. Experimentation or deeper investigation under the supervision of a faculty member of topics in mathematics that may be, but need not be, connected with an existing course. No one may receive more than seven semester hours of credit for this course. Formerly offered as MATH 290 .
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 7 total credits. 7 total completions.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Revisiting Real Numbers and Algebra
courses.description: Central to teaching precollege mathematics is the need for an in-depth understanding of real numbers and algebra. This course explores this content, emphasizing problem solving and mathematical reasoning.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Linear Algebra for Applications
courses.description: Algebra of matrices with applications: determinants, solution of linear systems by Gaussian elimination, Gram-Schmidt procedure, and eigenvalues. Previously offered as MATH 547.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Discrete Mathematics
courses.description: This course serves as a transition from computational to more theoretical mathematics. Topics are from the foundations of mathematics: logic, set theory, relations and functions, induction, permutations and combinations, recurrence. Honors version available.

courses.title: First Course in Differential Equations
courses.description: Introductory ordinary differential equations, first- and second-order differential equations with applications, higher-order linear equations, systems of first-order linear equations (introducing linear algebra as needed). Honors version available.

source.text: MATH 383. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisite, MATH 233 or MATH 235 .

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: First Course in Differential Equations Laboratory
courses.description: Course is computational laboratory component designed to help students visualize ODE solutions in Matlab. Emphasis is on differential equations motivated by applied sciences. Some applied linear algebra will appear as needed for computation and modeling purposes.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisite, MATH 233 or MATH 235; Pre- or corequisite, MATH 383.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Undergraduate Reading and Research in Mathematics
courses.description: Permission of the director of undergraduate studies. This course is intended mainly for students working on honors projects. No one may receive more than three semester hours credit for this course.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 6 total credits. 6 total completions.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Teaching and Learning Mathematics
courses.description: Study of how people learn and understand mathematics, based on research in mathematics, mathematics education, psychology, and cognitive science. This course is designed to prepare undergraduate mathematics majors to become excellent high school mathematics teachers. It involves field work in both the high school and college environments.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Introduction to Probability
courses.description: Introduction to mathematical theory of probability covering random variables; moments; binomial, Poisson, normal and related distributions; generating functions; sums and sequences of random variables; and statistical applications. Students may not receive credit for both STOR 435 and STOR 535 .
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisites, MATH/ STOR 235 or MATH 233; and STOR 215 or STOR 315 or MATH 381 or COMP 283.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Advanced Calculus I
courses.description: The real numbers, continuity and differentiability of functions of one variable, infinite series, integration. Honors version available.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisites, MATH 233 or MATH 235, and MATH 381; A grade of A- or better in STOR 215 may substitute for MATH 381.

source.text: MATH 521. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisites, MATH 233 or MATH 235 , and MATH 381 ; A grade of A- or better in STOR 215 may substitute for MATH 381 .

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Advanced Calculus II
courses.description: Functions of several variables, the derivative as a linear transformation, inverse and implicit function theorems, multiple integration. Honors version available.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Functions of a Complex Variable with Applications
courses.description: The algebra of complex numbers, elementary functions and their mapping properties, complex limits, power series, analytic functions, contour integrals, Cauchy's theorem and formulae, Laurent series and residue calculus, elementary conformal mapping and boundary value problems, Poisson integral formula for the disk and the half plane.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Elementary Differential Equations
courses.description: Linear differential equations, power series solutions, Laplace transforms, numerical methods.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Special Functions
courses.description: Bernoulli numbers and polynomials, Fourier series, Riemann zeta function. Gamma function, Bethe integrals, Stirling formula. Gauss sums, Jacobi sums. Hypergeometric functions. Singularities of differential equations. Orthogonal polynomials. Chebyshev polynomials. Applications.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisites, MATH 233 or 235; and MATH 347, and MATH 381.

source.text: MATH 525. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisites, MATH 233 or 235 ; and MATH 347 , and MATH 381 .

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Mathematical Methods for the Physical Sciences I
courses.description: Theory and applications of Laplace transform, Fourier series and transform, Sturm-Liouville problems. Students will be expected to do some numerical calculations on either a programmable calculator or a computer. This course has an optional computer laboratory component: MATH 528L .

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Laboratory for Mathematical Methods for the Physical Sciences I
courses.description: Training in the use of symbolic and numerical computing packages and their application to the MATH 528 lecture topics. Students will need a CCI-compatible computing device.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisite, MATH 383; pre- or corequisite, MATH 528.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Mathematical Methods for the Physical Sciences II
courses.description: Introduction to boundary value problems for the diffusion, Laplace and wave partial differential equations. Bessel functions and Legendre functions. Introduction to complex variables including the calculus of residues. This course has an optional computer laboratory component: MATH 529L .

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Laboratory for Mathematical Methods for the Physical Sciences II
courses.description: Training in the use of symbolic and numerical computing packages and their application to the MATH 529 lecture topics. Students will need a CCI-compatible computing device.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisite, MATH 383; pre- or corequisite, MATH 529.

courses.title: Elementary Theory of Numbers
courses.description: Divisibility, Euclidean algorithm, congruences, residue classes, Euler's function, primitive roots, Chinese remainder theorem, quadratic residues, number-theoretic functions, Farey and continued fractions, Gaussian integers.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Elements of Modern Algebra
courses.description: Binary operations, groups, subgroups, cosets, quotient groups, rings, polynomials.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Combinatorial Mathematics
courses.description: Counting selections, binomial identities, inclusion-exclusion, recurrences, Catalan numbers. Selected topics from algorithmic and structural combinatorics, or from applications to physics and cryptography.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Graph Theory
courses.description: Graphs: degree, isomorphisms, trees, connectivity, reliable networks. Eulerian and Hamiltonian cycles. Bipartite graphs, matching theory, applications in optimal assignments. Chromatic numbers and polynomials. Planar graphs, Kuratowski's theorem, Four-Color Theorem. Network flows.

source.text: MATH 549. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisites, MATH 347 and MATH 381 .

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Topology
courses.description: Introduction to topics in topology, particularly surface topology, including classification of compact surfaces, Euler characteristic, orientability, vector fields on surfaces, tessellations, and fundamental group.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisites, MATH 233 or MATH 235, and MATH 381.

source.text: MATH 550. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisites, MATH 233 or MATH 235 , and MATH 381 .

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Euclidean and Non-Euclidean Geometries
courses.description: Critical study of basic notions and models of Euclidean and non-Euclidean geometries: order, congruence, and distance.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisite, MATH 381; A grade of A- or better in STOR 215 may substitute for MATH 381.

source.text: MATH 551. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisite, MATH 381 ; A grade of A- or better in STOR 215 may substitute for MATH 381 .

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Differential Geometry of Curves and Surfaces
courses.description: Curves: arc length, curvature, global properties. Surfaces: smoothness, compactness, derivatives, tangent and normal vectors. Fundamental Forms: curvatures, covariant derivatives, non-Euclidean geometries, Theorema Egregium.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisites, MATH 233 or MATH 235, and MATH 347, and MATH 381.

source.text: MATH 552. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisites, MATH 233 or MATH 235 , and MATH 347 , and MATH 381 .

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Introduction to Dynamics
courses.description: Topics will vary and may include iteration of maps, orbits, periodic points, attractors, symbolic dynamics, bifurcations, fractal sets, chaotic systems, systems arising from differential equations, iterated function systems, and applications.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Optimization with Applications in Machine Learning
courses.description: This course will provide an introduction to convex optimization, including convex sets and functions, modeling, conic problems, optimality conditions and algorithms. The second part of the course will address non-convex problems, focusing on contemporary optimization challenges in large-scale optimization and practical approaches for machine learning and deep learning.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisites, MATH 233 or MATH 235, MATH 347 or MATH 577, and COMP 110 or COMP 116.

source.text: MATH 560. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisites, MATH 233 or MATH 235 , MATH 347 or MATH 577 , and COMP 110 or COMP 116 .

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Applied Linear Algebra for Scientific Computing and Data Science
courses.description: This course will introduce foundational mathematical concepts for scientific computing and machine learning through the lens of linear algebra. Topics will include a review of highlights of linear algebra, with a focus on the singular value decomposition, elements of numerical linear algebra, including iterative methods and pseudospectra, and special matrices, like those that appear in the Fourier transform and fundamental signal processing algorithms, and algorithms that take advantage of matrix structure, like multigrid methods.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisites, COMP 116 and one of MATH 347 or MATH 577.

source.text: MATH 561. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisites, COMP 116 and one of MATH 347 or MATH 577 .

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Introduction to Fluid Mechanics
courses.description: Mathematical methods applied to problems in fluid dynamics. Particular attention will be given to the power of dimensional analysis and scaling arguments. Topics will include: particle motion (e.g. the dynamics of sports balls), animal locomotion (e.g. swimming and flying), viscous flows (e.g. geological fluid dynamics), rotating and stratified flows (geophysical fluid dynamics), gravity currents and plumes (environmental fluid mechanics), drops, bubbles, and films.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Mathematical Modeling in the Life Sciences
courses.description: Requires some knowledge of computer programming. Model validation and numerical simulations using ordinary, partial, stochastic, and delay differential equations. Applications to the life sciences may include muscle physiology, biological fluid dynamics, neurobiology, molecular regulatory networks, and cell biology.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisites, MATH 383 and MATH 347 or MATH 577.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Introduction to Numerical Analysis
courses.description: Requires some knowledge of computer programming. Iterative methods, interpolation, polynomial and spline approximations, numerical differentiation and integration, numerical solution of ordinary and partial differential equations.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisites, MATH 383 and either MATH 577 or MATH 347.

source.text: MATH 566. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisites, MATH 383 and either MATH 577 or MATH 347 .

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Linear Algebra
courses.description: Vector spaces, linear transformations, duality, diagonalization, primary and cyclic decomposition, Jordan canonical form, inner product spaces, orthogonal reduction of symmetric matrices, spectral theorem, bilinear forms, multilinear functions. A much more abstract course than MATH 347 .
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisites, MATH 381 and 383; A grade of A- or better in STOR 215 may substitute for MATH 381.

source.text: MATH 577. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisites, MATH 381 and 383 ; A grade of A- or better in STOR 215 may substitute for MATH 381 .

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Algebraic Structures
courses.description: Permutation groups, matrix groups, groups of linear transformations, symmetry groups; finite abelian groups. Residue class rings, algebra of matrices, linear maps, and polynomials. Real and complex numbers, rational functions, quadratic fields, finite fields.

courses.title: Algebraic Geometry
courses.description: Algebraic curves: local and global properties. Tangent lines, smooth and singular points, intersection multiplicities. Projective curves, degree, Bezout's theorem. Dual curve, Plucker formulas. Complex numbers, some complex analysis, Riemann surfaces. Applications in control theory, robotics, error-correcting codes.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisites, MATH 233 or MATH 235, and MATH 347, and MATH 381.

source.text: MATH 579. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisites, MATH 233 or MATH 235 , and MATH 347 , and MATH 381 .

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Topics in Mathematics
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. Topics may focus on matrix theory, analysis, algebra, geometry, or applied and computational mathematics.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 12 total credits. 4 total completions.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Nonlinear Dynamics
courses.description: Interdisciplinary introduction to nonlinear dynamics and chaos. Fixed points, bifurcations, strange attractors, with applications to physics, biology, chemistry, finance.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisite, MATH 383; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Probability II
courses.description: Foundations of probability. Basic classical theorems. Modes of probabilistic convergence. Central limit problem. Generating functions, characteristic functions. Conditional probability and expectation.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisite, STOR 634; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Enumerative Combinatorics
courses.description: Basic counting; partitions; recursions and generating functions; signed enumeration; counting with respect to symmetry, plane partitions, and tableaux.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Combinatorial Structures
courses.description: Graph theory, matchings, Ramsey theory, extremal set theory, network flows, lattices, Moebius inversion, q-analogs, combinatorial and projective geometries, codes, and designs.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Introductory Analysis
courses.description: Requires knowledge of advanced calculus. Elementary metric space topology, continuous functions, differentiation of vector-valued functions, implicit and inverse function theorems. Topics from Weierstrass theorem, existence and uniqueness theorems for differential equations, series of functions.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Complex Analysis
courses.description: A rigorous treatment of complex integration, including the Cauchy theory. Elementary special functions, power series, local behavior of analytic functions.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Qualitative Theory of Differential Equations
courses.description: Requires knowledge of linear algebra. Existence and uniqueness theorems, linear and nonlinear systems, differential equations in the plane and on surfaces, Poincare-Bendixson theory, Lyapunov stability and structural stability, critical point analysis.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Scientific Computation I
courses.description: Requires some programming experience and basic numerical analysis. Error in computation, solutions of nonlinear equations, interpolation, approximation of functions, Fourier methods, numerical integration and differentiation, introduction to numerical solution of ODEs, Gaussian elimination.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Scientific Computation II
courses.description: Theory and practical issues arising in linear algebra problems derived from physical applications, e.g., discretization of ODEs and PDEs. Linear systems, linear least squares, eigenvalue problems, singular value decomposition.

source.text: MATH 662. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisite, MATH 661 . | COMP 662 , ENVR 662 .

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Applied Stochastic Processes
courses.description: Requires an undergraduate course in differential equations and linear algebra; some knowledge of probability and programming experience is recommended. Modeling, analysis, and simulation of stochastic processes with an emphasis on applications from biology, physics, and data science. Intended for students both within math and adjacent fields with a quantitative background. Stochastic processes covered include: Poisson process, discrete and continuous time Markov chains, and Stochastic differential equations.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Methods of Applied Mathematics I
courses.description: Requires an undergraduate course in differential equations. Contour integration, asymptotic expansions, steepest descent/stationary phase methods, special functions arising in physical applications, elliptic and theta functions, elementary bifurcation theory.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Methods of Applied Mathematics II
courses.description: Perturbation methods for ODEs and PDEs, WKBJ method, averaging and modulation theory for linear and nonlinear wave equations, long-time asymptotics of Fourier integral representations of PDEs, Green's functions, dynamical systems tools.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Modules, Linear Algebra, and Groups
courses.description: Requires knowledge of linear algebra and algebraic structures. Modules over rings, canonical forms for linear operators and bilinear forms, multilinear algebra, groups and group actions.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 6 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Groups, Representations, and Fields
courses.description: Internal structure of groups, Sylow theorems, generators and relations, group representations, fields, Galois theory, category theory.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Differentiable Manifolds
courses.description: Calculus on manifolds, vector bundles, vector fields and differential equations, de Rham cohomology.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Introductory Topology
courses.description: Topology. Point set topology, metric spaces, connectedness, compactness. Classification of surfaces. Homotopy theory, the fundamental group, covering spaces, Brouwer fixed-point theorem. Simplicial homology, homology groups.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Topics In Mathematics
courses.description: Permission of the department. Directed study of an advanced topic in mathematics. Topics will vary.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 12 total credits. 4 total completions.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Honors Research in Mathematics
courses.description: Permission of the director of undergraduate studies. Readings in mathematics and the beginning of directed research on an honors thesis.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Honors Thesis in Mathematics
courses.description: Permission of the director of undergraduate studies. Completion of an honors thesis under the direction of a member of the faculty. Required of all candidates for graduation with honors in mathematics.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Introduction to Partial Differential Equations
courses.description: Basic methods in partial differential equations. Topics may include: Cauchy-Kowalewski Theorem, Holmgren's Uniqueness Theorem, Laplace's equation, Maximum Principle, Dirichlet problem, harmonic functions, wave equation, heat equation.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Measure and Integration
courses.description: Lebesgue and abstract measure and integration, convergence theorems, differentiation, Radon-Nikodym theorem, product measures, Fubini theorem, Lebesgue spaces, invariance under transformations, Haar measure and convolution.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisite, MATH 653; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite.

items.text: permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite

source.text: MATH 753. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisite, MATH 653 ; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Introductory Functional Analysis
courses.description: Hahn-Banach and separation theorems. Normed and locally convex spaces, duals of spaces and maps, weak topologies; closed graph and open mapping theorems, uniform boundedness theorem, linear operators. Spring.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Advanced Complex Analysis
courses.description: Laurent series; Mittag-Leffler and Weierstrass Theorems; Riemann mapping theorem; Runge's theorem; additional topics chosen from: harmonic, elliptic, univalent, entire, meromorphic functions; Dirichlet problem; Riemann surfaces.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Several Complex Variables
courses.description: Elementary theory, the Cousin problems, domains of holomorphy, Runge domains and polynomial approximation, local theory, complex analytic structures, coherent analytic sheaves and Stein manifolds, Cartan's theorems.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Spectral Theory
courses.description: Hilbert spaces, unbounded linear operators, symmetric and essentially self-adjoint operators, the Cayley transform and von Neumann's theorem for self-adjoint extensions of symmetric operators, spectrum and resolvent set, analytic Fredholm theorem, spectral theorems for unitary and self-adjoint operators, the Borel functional calculus and Stone's formula, spectral measures, decompositions of the spectrum, Weyl criterion and stability, and the RAGE theorem.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Semiclassical Analysis
courses.description: Fourier analysis, pseudo-differential operators, symbol calculus, classical-quantum correspondence, the damped wave equation, eigenfunctions and asymptotics.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Numerical ODE/PDE, I
courses.description: Single, multistep methods for ODEs: stability regions, the root condition; stiff systems, backward difference formulas; two-point BVPs; stability theory; finite difference methods for linear advection diffusion equations.

source.text: MATH 761. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisites, MATH 661 and 662 . | ENVR 761 , MASC 781 .

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Numerical ODE/PDE, II
courses.description: Elliptic equation methods (finite differences, elements, integral equations); hyperbolic conservation law methods (Lax-Fiedrich, characteristics, entropy condition, shock tracking/capturing); spectral, pseudo-spectral methods; particle methods, fast summation, fast multipole/vortex methods.

source.text: MATH 762. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisite, MATH 761 . | ENVR 762 , EMES 782 .

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Mathematical Modeling I
courses.description: Nondimensionalization and identification of leading order physical effects with respect to relevant scales and phenomena; derivation of classical models of fluid mechanics (lubrication, slender filament, thin films, Stokes flow); derivation of weakly nonlinear envelope equations. Fall.

source.text: MATH 768. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisites, MATH 661 , 662 , 668 , and 669 . | ENVR 763 , MASC 783 .

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Mathematical Modeling II
courses.description: Current models in science and technology: topics ranging from material science applications (e.g., flow of polymers and LCPs); geophysical applications (e.g., ocean circulation, quasi-geostrophic models, atmospheric vortices).

source.text: MATH 769. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisites, MATH 661 , 662 , 668 , and 669 . | ENVR 764 , EMES 784 .

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Commutative Algebra
courses.description: Field extensions, integral ring extensions, Nullstellensatz and normalization theorem, derivations and separability, local rings, valuations, completions, filtrations and graded rings, dimension theory.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Lie Groups
courses.description: Lie groups, closed subgroups, Lie algebra of a Lie group, exponential map, compact groups, Haar measure, orthogonality relations, Peter-Weyl theorem, maximal torus, representations, Weyl character formula, homogeneous spaces.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Lie Algebras
courses.description: Nilpotent, solvable, and semisimple Lie algebras, structure theorems, root systems, Weyl groups, weights, classification of semisimple Lie algebras and their finite dimensional representations, character formulas.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Algebraic Geometry
courses.description: Topics may include: algebraic varieties, algebraic functions, abelian varieties, projective and complete varieties, algebraic groups, schemes and the Grothendieck theory, Riemann-Roch theorem.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Algebraic Topology
courses.description: Homotopy and homology; simplicial complexes and singular homology; other topics may include cohomology, universal coefficient theorems, higher homotopy groups, fibre spaces.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Differential Geometry
courses.description: Riemannian geometry, first and second variation of area and applications, effect of curvature on homology and homotopy, Chern-Weil theory of characteristic classes, Chern-Gauss-Bonnet theorem.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Symplectic Geometry
courses.description: Symplectic forms, Moser and Darboux Theorems. Hamiltonian and classical mechanics, Euler-Lagrange equations. Moment maps and symplectic reduction.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Harmonic Analysis
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. Subjects may include topological groups, abstract harmonic analysis, Fourier analysis, noncommutative harmonic analysis and group representation, automorphic forms, and analytic number theory.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Advanced Functional Analysis
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. Subjects may include operator theory on Hilbert space, operators on Banach spaces, locally convex spaces, vector measures, Banach algebras.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Theory of Dynamical Systems
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. Topics may include: ergodic theory, topological dynamics, stability theory of differential equations, classical dynamical systems, differentiable dynamics.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Special Topics
courses.description: Advance topics in current research in statistics and operations research.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Topics in Computational Mathematics
courses.description: Topics may include: finite element method; numerical methods for hyperbolic conservation laws, infinite dimensional optimization problems, variational inequalities, inverse problems.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Topics in Algebra
courses.description: Topics from the theory of rings, theory of bialgebras, homological algebra, algebraic number theory, categories and functions.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Topics in Combinatorial Mathematics
courses.description: Topics may include: combinatorial geometries, coloring and the critical problem, the bracket algebra, reduced incidence algebras and generating functions, binomial enumeration, designs, valuation module of a lattice, lattice theory.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisite, MATH 641; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Special Topics in Geometry
courses.description: Topics may include elliptic operators, complex manifolds, exterior differential systems, homogeneous spaces, integral geometry, submanifolds of Euclidean space, geometrical aspects of mathematical physics.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Topics in Algebraic Topology
courses.description: Topics primarily from algebraic or differential topology, such as cohomology operations, homotopy groups, fibre bundles, spectral sequences, K-theory, cobordism, Morse Theory, surgery, topology of singularities.

courses.title: Seminar and Directed Readings
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics.

courses.title: Practical Training Course in Mathematics
courses.description: Required preparation, passed Ph.D. or M.S. written comprehensive exam. An opportunity for the practical training of a graduate student interested in mathematics is identified. Typically this opportunity is expected to take the form of a summer internship.
